name: Celtic No. 2 Seven-Point 1897
designer: Unidentified in the consulted historical specimens
foundry: Farmer, as credited in the Government Printing Office document specimen
description: The seven-point Celtic No. 2 cut, preserving its optical proportions, bowed crossbars and flowing figures.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z capitals, all ten figures and period. Space is a modern layout advance. Lowercase and unsupported punctuation are not encoded.
observed: All 26 capitals, ten figures and the declared punctuation are observed in the seven-point Celtic No. 2 cut. Exact selected impressions, native comparisons and measurements accompany the master. The 1904 document specimen credits Farmer.
reconstructed: No visible characters invented. Spacing, digital metrics, paper illumination correction and measured rigid rotations are modern preparation choices.
